programme: EP300 and KAT7 are lysine acetyltransferase coactivators (p300/MYST-family) that here are read out through two distinct sequence-specific partners: REL (NF-κB) in one disease, and a cluster of fusion-oncoprotein partners — TFCP2, CREB3L1, MEF2D, KDM2B — in the other. The acetyltransferase node is the recurring hub; the transcription factor it is coupled to differs by tissue.
role_in_a: In COPD, REL/NF-κB drives chronic inflammatory transcription in airway tissue (IL6, TNF, CXCL8, IL1B are among REL's target set here), directly supported by PMID 40508027 on NF-κB subunit c-Rel in COPD; EP300 and KAT7 are the canonical acetyltransferase coactivators of NF-κB-driven transcription, though no retrieved paper places them in COPD specifically.
role_in_b: In sarcoma, KAT7/HBO1 is independently reported as oncogenic in osteosarcoma (PMID 33754016), and EP300 is implicated in synovial sarcoma (PMID 42192525) and an EP300::VGLL3 rhabdomyoblastic fusion tumor (PMID 41649512). TFCP2, CREB3L1, MEF2D and KDM2B are recurrent partners in disease-defining gene fusions (FUS/EWSR1::TFCP2, EWSR1::CREB3L1, MEF2D::NCOA2, KDM2B fusions) that create aberrant lineage-defining transcription factors in rare sarcoma subtypes.
shared_axis: Both diseases exploit the same acetylation-based coactivator machinery (EP300/KAT7) but couple it to a different disease-specific transcription factor — REL for chronic inflammatory gene induction in airway disease, and FET-fusion partner TFs for aberrant lineage transcription in sarcoma. The convergence is on the coactivator, not on a shared disease programme.
reasoning: Each side of the module is independently documented — REL in COPD, and KAT7/EP300/TFCP2/CREB3L1/MEF2D/KDM2B in sarcoma — so each disease is separately known to touch this acetyltransferase-coactivator axis. But the specific COPD leg of the mechanism (EP300 or KAT7 acting on NF-κB in airway tissue) is not itself evidenced in the retrieved material; it rests on general acetyltransferase biology rather than a COPD-specific citation, so the account is supported but not established for this pair.
support: PMID 40508027 (REL/c-Rel discussed in COPD and NF-κB biology); PMID 33754016 (KAT7/HBO1 oncogenic in osteosarcoma); PMID 42192525 (EP300 in TGF-β/p300 pathway, synovial sarcoma); PMID 41649512 (EP300::VGLL3 fusion rhabdomyoblastic tumor); PMID 42678417, 41497928, 41552649, 41640459 (TFCP2 fusions in rhabdomyosarcoma/soft tissue sarcoma); PMID 42100950, 42501102, 42433341, 42067069 (CREB3L1/EWSR1 fusions in fibrosarcoma and related soft tissue tumors); PMID 40057039 (MEF2D::NCOA2 fusion tumor); PMID 40865919 (KDM2B fusions in uterine sarcoma); PMID 38380509 (REL/BPTF axis in Kaposi sarcoma, weak tie-in).
how_to_falsify: In primary COPD airway epithelial/immune cells versus controls, run ChIP-seq/CUT&RUN for EP300 and KAT7 co-occupancy with REL(p65) at inflammatory promoters (IL6, CXCL8, TNF); if the acetyltransferases do not co-localize with REL there, or EP300/KAT7 knockdown fails to blunt REL-driven induction, the shared-coactivator link fails. In parallel, in fusion-positive sarcoma lines (TFCP2-fusion rhabdomyosarcoma, EWSR1::CREB3L1 fibrosarcoma, MEF2D::NCOA2 tumor), test whether EP300/KAT7 HAT-domain inhibition selectively collapses the fusion-TF transcriptional signature and viability relative to fusion-negative controls; failure to do so undercuts the claim that these fusion TFs act through this same coactivator node.
caveats: Tissue pairing (lung vs. soft tissue) is anatomically unrelated, and no explicit tissue-generic exclusion list was supplied for this pair, so tissue-genericity of EP300/KAT7 could not be screened against a provided baseline. Support for the sarcoma-side fusion factors (TFCP2, CREB3L1, MEF2D, KDM2B) comes largely from rare case reports/small case series on individual fusion subtypes, not cohort-level validation. The COPD-side evidence rests on a single factor (REL) plus one indirect KAT7-osteosarcoma or EP300-sarcoma citation; the acetyltransferase role in COPD itself is inferred, not retrieved. Five other concordant factors (PITX3, NR2C2, CEBPB, TFDP3, PPARGC1B) had no supporting citations in either disease and are excluded from the programme rather than forced into the story. Excluded single-view factors (KLF3, TCF15, TAL1, JUND, HES4, MIXL1, MED1, CXXC1, IRF2BPL, HOXA10, SMARCC1, CEBPG) topped one patient group each but did not generalize, and are correctly left out of this account.
